headline: Intimate venues, eminent musicians
summary: Kitchen parties, a cello recital, Night Music in the dark, and finales in Clare and Yarmouth with the world premiere of Derek Charke’s *Harvest Dusk*.
intro: Our goal in producing this festival has always been to create something truly meaningful for our region: an event that celebrates world-class artistry while staying deeply rooted in community. We believe that great music shouldn’t be confined to big cities or concert halls. It should be something everyone can experience, regardless of age, background, or income.

That’s why this festival isn’t just about concerts. It’s about free performances in schools and long-term care homes, bilingual programming that reflects our Acadian heritage, and open rehearsals held in public spaces where people can experience the creative process up close. It’s about artists meeting audiences. Not from a distance, but in shared spaces, as neighbours.
scheduleNote: The festival also included free open rehearsals at the Yarmouth Mall and Third Cup Café, a panel discussion with the musicians at the Yarmouth Waterfront Gallery, and free performances in schools and long-term care homes.

events.title: Festival Kitchen Party I
description: Meet the festival quartet and hear them play works by your favorite composers. Dessert will be served. Very limited seating - exact location in town (Yarmouth) will be disclosed after tickets are purchased.
*What to expect*
- Music in a private, welcoming home setting
- Conversation and connection with the musicians — ask questions, hear the stories behind the music, and even choose what the musicians play!
- A relaxed atmosphere that blends the warmth of a Nova Scotian kitchen party with the beauty of chamber music
- Dessert will be served

The most unique part of the evening is that you get to choose the program. Festival Artistic Director and violist David Yang will bring a stack of string quartets followed by lively voting from the attendees on which composer they want the musicians to play: it's sight reading as a contact sport!

events.title: Eliana Razzino Yang in Recital

events.title: Night Music: Music in the Dark
description: The music of Bach, Barber, Haydn, Ravel, Arvo Pärt and more performed by the Festival Quartet in near-darkness! Lowered visual stimulation increases aural sensitivity for a truly memorable experience.

An experience unlike any other festival concert. Imagine entering a beautiful Gothic mortuary chapel. The lights go down. The quartet begins to play. There is almost nothing to see. The music has not been announced beforehand. With visual stimulation deliberately reduced, your ears become more sensitive to every sound, every silence, every breath and every movement of the music.

events.title: Grand Finale in Clare
description: The musicians have been rehearsing all week and are ready to delight the audience at this concert in Clare with a program of works by Josef Haydn, György Kurtág, Maurice Ravel and a world premiere, composed for our inaugural festival by Juno and ECMA award-winning composer Derek Charke.
Music is a language of its own, but the introductions and description of the pieces will all be done in French for this performance.
On a tellement hâte de vous voir!
